To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is an exact correspondence between the dynamics of minimally and non- minimally coupled models, 2) the dynamics of the minimally coupled model is simpler than the one of the non-minimally one, 3) the non-minimallly coupled models are integrable and can exhibit a bounce.
we have found a new integrable model of the Universe, which is a generalization of the model found in the paper [Phys. Rev. D 85, 123528 (2012)].
we have found a set of integrable scalar field cosmological models with non-minimal coupling and that the relation between minimally and non- minimally coupled models is not trivial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation between integrable cosmologies with minimally and non- minimally coupled scalar fields.
the study of a class of integrable models in the Jordan frame.
a systematic study of the relation between the integrability of a cosmological model and the existence of bounces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class of models we are considering is a good candidate for a cosmological theory with a bouncing behaviour.
the integrability of a cosmological model with minimal coupling is not necessarily a sufficient condition for the integrability of the same model with non-minimal coupling.
the class of models we have investigated can be generalized to a larger class of integrable models which can be solved exactly and exhibit bounces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the integrable cosmological model with minimal coupling is a special case of a more general class of integrable models with non-minimal coupling and the dynamics of the latter can be reduced to that of the former by a conformal transformation.

the integrable models we considered are related to the integrable models of the Einstein frame by means of a conformal transformation, but they are not related to the same class of models of the Jordan frame.
the non-minimally interacting models can be obtained from the minimally interacting ones by means of a conformal transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for some particular models, the existence of a bounce in the Jordan frame implies a bounce in the Einstein frame.
the existence of bounces in the Einstein frame does not imply the existence of bounc- es in the Jordan frame and viceversa.
the existence of a bounce in the Jordan frame is a necessary condition for the existence of bounces in the Einstein frame.
